title: "Setup"

## R and packages

**R.** The project needs R 4.6.1 (the version in `renv.lock`) with a toolchain
that can build R packages from source. If you are using a SLURM cluster, you 
may have luck using spack for this. See
[this example](https://github.com/BrentLab/htcf_spack_rstudio_server) of 
setting up a R environment for rstudio server and R 4.6.1 via spack

**R packages** come from the project's renv library (`renv.lock`). renv activates
automatically from `.Rprofile` when R starts in the project directory. From a
fresh clone:

```r
options(renv.install.timeout = 6 * 3600)
renv::restore()
```
If this is a completely fresh installation with none of these packages already 
installed, this can take hours. Additionally, note the following:

- **The renv cache.** renv links packages from its cache (`~/.cache/R/renv`)
  when a matching
  build is there, so a restore on a machine that has built them before takes
  minutes, not hours.
- **Interrupted installs** leave `00LOCK-<package>` directories in the project
  library, and installing that package then fails until they are removed.
- **The timeout.** Many packages build from source (roughly 300 on the cluster
  this project was developed on, hours of build time). renv's default deadline
  for a whole install is one hour, and when it's reached renv rolls back the
  entire batch. Finished builds stay in renv's cache, so a re-run picks up
  where it stopped.
- **`.Rprofile` turns off two renv start-up checks**, `synchronized.check`
  (a scan of every project file, about a minute on a network filesystem) and
  the sandbox (about 40 s on a network filesystem when 20 workers start at
  once). Together they took every worker's R start-up from 68 s to about 10 s.
  Run `renv::status()` by hand when you want the check.

### CoGAPS and ProjectR need to be installed from github

1. **CoGAPS is installed from a patched local checkout, not a repository.** Its
  committed `configure` leaves the autoconf-archive OpenMP macros unexpanded
  ([FertigLab/CoGAPS#150](https://github.com/FertigLab/CoGAPS/issues/150)), so
  built as-is it compiles single-threaded without saying so. The upstream fix
  ([#151](https://github.com/FertigLab/CoGAPS/pull/151)) only changes their
  Dockerfile, so regenerate `configure` before installing:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/FertigLab/CoGAPS.git logs/build/CoGAPS
git -C logs/build/CoGAPS checkout f9075096   # master as installed (3.33.2), after #151
export ACLOCAL_PATH=<the aclocal directory that holds autoconf-archive's macros>
(cd logs/build/CoGAPS && autoreconf -fi)
Rscript -e 'renv::install(normalizePath("logs/build/CoGAPS"))'
Rscript -e 'library(CoGAPS); stopifnot(compiledWithOpenMPSupport())'
```

`autoreconf` needs `autoconf-archive`: install it with your system's package manager and point
`ACLOCAL_PATH` at the `aclocal` directory that holds its macros.

2. **projectR is the `feature-add_center_by_loadings` branch** of
[cmatKhan/projectR](https://github.com/cmatKhan/projectR/tree/feature-add_center_by_loadings).
It adds `center_by_loadings`, used to project PCA fits. renv records it as a
GitHub remote, so `renv::restore()` installs it.

## Raw data

Dataset configs give data paths relative to a data root: `data_root` in
`config/pipeline.yml` (eg, `/scratch/mblab/chasem/hf_sepsis_collection`),
overridden by the `SEPSIS_DATA_ROOT` environment variable. See [Data](data.qmd).

## Developer notes

### Claude

Claude was used extensively to develop this project.

### Building these docs

The site is a [Quarto](https://quarto.org) website in `docs/`. Quarto ships with
RStudio Server (`.../rstudio-server/bin/quarto/bin/quarto`); elsewhere, install
it from quarto.org.

```sh
quarto render docs      # writes docs/_site/
quarto preview docs     # live preview while editing
```

Rendering first runs `docs/build_reference.R`, which builds the
[Function reference](reference.qmd) from the roxygen comments in the code (it needs the
project's `roxygen2`).

### Documenting functions

Every function carries a standard [roxygen](https://roxygen2.r-lib.org) block: a title line,
a description, `@param` for each argument and `@return`. This is a project, not a package,
so there are no `man/` pages; the blocks feed the reference page instead.

```r
#' Stable identity for a fit
#'
#' Dataset + method + parameters, excluding resource-only settings.
#'
#' @param dataset_id Dataset id.
#' @param method Method name.
#' @param params Flattened parameter list (`flatten_params()`).
#' @param resource_params Parameter names left out of the identity.
#' @return The fit key, `"<method>_<16 hex characters>"`.
fit_key <- function(dataset_id, method, params, resource_params = character(0)) { ... }
```

Comments never change targets' hashes, so documenting a function never reruns anything.
